subject.title: Add multi-gateway cron job coordination for HA deployments

question: Should distributed cron ownership be implemented as a core feature, a plugin-provided coordination API, or folded into the broader horizontal-scaling/runtime architecture work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend boundary, config shape, failure semantics, health/CLI surface, and relationship to broader HA architecture require maintainer product and architecture intent.

options.title: Design backend-neutral ownership
options.body: Define a generic cron lease or leader contract before implementation so Redis, etcd, DynamoDB, or SQLite-backed deployments do not become competing one-off paths.

options.title: Fold into broader HA design
options.body: Make this issue a cron-specific requirement of the horizontal-scaling or distributed-runtime work and close it only after that design explicitly owns cron scheduling.

options.title: Document external-only operation
options.body: If built-in HA cron coordination is out of scope, document external schedulers or external lock patterns as the supported deployment model.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral ownership
recommendation.body: Define a generic cron lease or leader contract before implementation so Redis, etcd, DynamoDB, or SQLite-backed deployments do not become competing one-off paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent cron scheduler history in the inspected evidence and already provided prior architecture-review context on this issue.
